results.title: The subgroup $2^kA$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an abelian group $A$, written additively, and a natural number $k$, $2^kA$ is the subgroup $\{2^k a : a \in A\}$ of $A$, the image of multiplication by $2^k$.

results.title: The two-power layer $2^{j-1}A / 2^jA$
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For an abelian group $A$, written additively, and a natural number $j$, this is the quotient group $2^{j-1}A / 2^jA$, where $2^kA$ denotes the subgroup $\{2^k a : a \in A\}$ and $2^jA \subseteq 2^{j-1}A$. For $j = 0$, where $j - 1$ is read as $0$, it is the trivial quotient $A / A$.

results.title: The $2^j$-rank of a finite abelian group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite abelian group, written additively, and let $j \ge 1$ be an integer. Writing $2^kA$ for the subgroup $\{2^k a : a \in A\}$, the $2^j$-rank of $A$ is the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_2$ of the quotient $2^{j-1}A / 2^jA$, which is an $\mathbb{F}_2$-vector space because $2$ kills it.

results.title: The $4$-rank of a finite abelian group
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a finite abelian group $A$, written additively, the $4$-rank of $A$ is the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_2$ of the quotient $2A / 4A$, where $2A = \{2a : a \in A\}$ and $4A = \{4a : a \in A\}$; it is the $2^j$-rank of $A$ for $j = 2$.

results.title: Generalized Fibonacci polynomials
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given polynomials $p_0, p_1, d, g \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$, the generalized Fibonacci polynomial sequence $(G_n)_{n \ge 0}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ is defined by $G_0 = p_0$, $G_1 = p_1$ and $G_{n+2} = d \, G_{n+1} + g \, G_n$ for every natural number $n$.

results.title: Index-one term of a generalized Fibonacci polynomial sequence

results.title: Recurrence for generalized Fibonacci polynomials

results.title: The Gibbs density is stationary

results.title: A zero-flux density determines the drift
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Rotational drifts share the Gibbs stationary density
results.caption: Theorem

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An explicit rotational drift with nonzero flux (our derivation): on `ℝ²` with `Ψ(x) = (x₀² + x₁²) / 2`, `D = 1` and the rotation generator `A = [[0, 1], [-1, 0]]`, the drift `-(∇Ψ + A ∇Ψ)` has the Gibbs (standard Gaussian, up to normalization) density as a stationary density, yet its flux at `(1, 0)` is nonzero, so it is not the gradient drift.

results.title: Shor's order-to-factor reduction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$, $a$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $N > 1$ and $a \ge 1$. Suppose $a^r \equiv 1 \pmod{N}$, $r$ is even, $a^{r/2} \not\equiv 1 \pmod{N}$ and $a^{r/2} \not\equiv -1 \pmod{N}$. Then $d = \gcd(a^{r/2} - 1, N)$, the value computed by the classical post-processing, is a nontrivial factor of $N$: $d$ divides $N$ and $1 < d < N$.
